casos.pergunta: What Rozanov said about Chernyshevsky?
casos.resposta_esperada: Rozanov treated Chernyshevsky ironically and with a certain distaste. He discovered in What Is to Be Done? traces of male homosocial desire that resonated more powerfully in the fin de siècle than in the earlier 1860s. Rozanov claimed that, without knowing it, Chernyshevsky deployed triangulated desire as love “between men,” which psychopathologists considered a symptom of degeneration.
